title: Beliefs
lead: Beliefs are the sixth of the seven ideas, and they cover what people accept as true about the world.

p: Beliefs are ideas people accept as true about the world. They are learned through experience and socialisation and may differ within one society.
In plain words, a belief is something a person thinks is true about the world.

writers.name: Interactionists
writers.says: examine how beliefs develop through experiences and discussions with others.

list: A student who believes that qualifications are the best route to a good job holds a belief about how the world works.
Her friend believes that practical experience matters more, so two people in one society can hold different beliefs.
The beliefs that families explain behind their celebrations are ideas that they accept as true.
Family advice may shape choices such as university or an apprenticeship, and the item links these choices to what each student believes about work.
Some pupils believe that influencers on social media always tell the truth about the products they promote, while others believe that they are paid to say it.
A person who believes that a black cat crossing their path brings bad luck holds a belief that many other people do not accept.

p: Define the term: Beliefs are ideas people accept as true about the world. They are learned through experience and socialisation and may differ within one society.
Item link: The students in the item hold different beliefs about what leads to a good job, one trusting qualifications and the other practical experience.
Explain with an example: Family advice may shape choices such as university or an apprenticeship. A belief about how to succeed differs from a value about what matters, such as valuing education.
Theory link: Interactionists examine how beliefs develop through experiences and discussions with others.

quote.t: One student believes qualifications are the best route to a good job, while her friend believes practical experience matters more. Their families encourage different choices after school.
